rationale:
**Applies.** `load_definitions` (src/evidence.rs:149-165) declares a local `let mut errors = Vec::new();` and collects repository-validation errors in it. It is a site under the `error_accumulators` query. It is not authoring code that collects errors only to abort, because it returns them as a report (an `InvalidData` error whose message is the joined `errors`).

**Obligations.** After a check fails, a site must still run every later check that doesn't depend on the failed check's result. It must also not report one failure twice.
- `book_source_dir(&root, &mut errors)` records a book.toml problem and falls back to `root.join("md")`. It returns a `PathBuf` rather than a `Result`, so a failure there cannot skip the next step.
- `collect_definitions(&root, &md_root, &mut errors)` then always runs. I read it, and it keeps going after failures. Unreadable chapters, invalid names, unsupported options, empty text and duplicates are each pushed to `errors` and followed by `continue` or fall-through, not by an early return. The only `?`-style exits in it are the `continue`s that skip just the failed item. Each of those pushes its own error first, so later independent checks, including the later per-definition loop, still run.
- The function uses no `?` or `return` after `errors` exists. It returns once at the end, so it doesn't stop short of any later check. Each failure is pushed once.

**Violation match `fs::canonicalize(root)?` (line 153).** This does not break the requirement here.
- It runs before `errors` exists and before any check has run, so no earlier failed check is being skipped past.
- Every later check needs the canonical root: `book_source_dir`, `collect_definitions`, and path display. They depend on its result, so the requirement does not require them to run if it fails.
- It also can't duplicate an error. It propagates a single `io::Error` and nothing else has been reported.

No gaps.

text: Repository validation MUST continue after a failed check and report every failed
check it finds in one run, each as a {term}`requirements.ci.validation_error`.
This is a convention for every validation error; the requirement for each check
states which conditions that check reports. A file that cannot be parsed, such as
a malformed `habeas.toml`, `book.toml`, or evidence file, is one failed check:
its error MAY report only the first parse or decoding problem in that file, and
checks that do not depend on its contents MUST still run.
The code that sequences the repository's checks carries out the first paragraph.
A repository-validation function that collects validation errors MUST hold them
in a parameter or local variable named `errors`, and a function with such a
variable is a site below; authoring code that collects errors only to abort is
not one. After one of its checks fails, a site MUST still run every later check
that does not depend on the failed check's result, including later checks in the
same loop iteration, and MUST NOT report one failure twice.
